notes.title: v1.0.11
notes.content: [p]The game has been patched to balance a few upgrades.[/p][h1]Changes[/h1][list][*][p]Banana's area increment is now 10% (instead of 5%)[/p][/*][*][p]Bomb's fuse decrement is now 0.025 seconds (instead of 0.1 seconds)[/p][/*][*][p]Bomb's cooldown decrement is now 1 second (instead of 0.8 seconds)[/p][/*][*][p]Rubber Band's base damage is now 300 (instead of 250)[/p][/*][*][p]Rubber Band's damage increment is now 150 (instead of 125)[/p][/*][*][p]Wheel's cooldown is now 10 seconds (instead of 5 seconds)[/p][/*][*][p]Wheel's cooldown decrement is now 1 second (instead of 0.5 seconds)[/p][/*][*][p]XP dots outside the bounds of the maze are now auto-collected[/p][/*][/list][h1]Balance Reasoning[/h1][p]Banana, while powerful at high levels, felt lacking at low levels. Doubling the area increment will make more than a single level in Banana more [strike]appeeling[/strike] appealing.[/p][p]Not being able to reduce Bomb's cooldown below 2.4 seconds was a calculation oversight on my part. Some players also correctly pointed out that reducing the fuse timer to 0.1 seconds made the upgrade less powerful, since it hit fewer enemies on average. These changes will help make Bomb more powerful when putting several levels in it.[/p][p]Rubber Band was not very powerful even when slowing down to try and get maximum value out of it. These damage increases will reward players for using Rubber Band efficiently.[/p][p]Wheel, when used effectively, was simply too powerful. I still want the playstyle to be possible, but players shouldn't be able to select Speedy and run a single direction all game. Doubling the cooldown at level 1 will make Wheel runs less trivial.[/p][p]Please let me know your thoughts either in the comments or in the [url="https://trampolinetales.com/discord"]official discord[/url]![/p][p]-Dan[/p][p]P.S. Eagle-eyed players may notice we skipped a version number. In actuality, v1.0.10 was only seen by internal testers and just had changes for the upcoming mobile version. If it appears that a version number was skipped, it's going to be for a reason like that going forward.[/p]

notes.title: Maze Mice is a new roguelike from the developer that inspired Balatro's creation
notes.content:
Every few weeks, I load up the climactic orchestral montage from The Game Awards 2024 and get a little misty-eyed as the Balatro theme kicks in. The deckbuilding sensation is a rousing success story, even claiming our own end-of-year top spot, and its creator 'Localthunk' has been keen to share the love around. Their latest target is developer Dan Dilorio of Trampoline Tales, who Localthunk cites as the leading inspiration for Balatro's creation, and whose new action roguelike Maze Mice has just launched on Steam, with a big 30% discount if you jump on it quickly.

notes.title: The Dream Update - Exiting Early Access!
notes.content: [p]Maze Mice has exited Early Access! With this update comes 154 unlockable achievements, a dynamic maze, and a new boss fight mechanic.[/p][h1]News[/h1][p]Hey everyone! As [url="https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/3385370/view/518589674441148930"]previously announced[/url], Maze Mice is fully releasing with this update. I can now say I'm satisfied with the game and feel it's ready to be called "v1.0." I'll never say never to adding more content, but that's relatively unlikely given the game hasn't made back its development costs.[/p][p]I realize the game only being in Early Access for about two months looks a little strange. The main reason for this is that my talented collaborators on this project got work done [i]much[/i] faster than I thought they would. A good problem to have![/p][p]I had decided Mace Mice's Early Access release date pretty far in advance, but rather than doing Early Access at all, the smarter decision probably would've been to wait a few months and release the game normally. I still have a lot to learn about being an independent game developer, but I get to do that thanks to all of your support![/p][p]I appreciate all of you sticking with me as I learn and improve, and I apologize for any confusion caused by the short Early Access period.[/p][p]-Dan[/p][h1]New Content[/h1][list][*][p]Added a dynamic unlockable maze[/p][/*][*][p]Added 154 unlockable achievements[/p][/*][*][p]Added an HP bar to the Boss[/p][/*][/list][h1]Game Balance[/h1][list][*][p]Each Boss life now has 1,000 more HP[/p][/*][*][p]Collecting big XP dots now deals 500 damage to the boss[/p][/*][/list][h1]Balance Reasoning[/h1][p]These changes were primarily implemented to encourage players to collect big XP dots -- and as a result, spawn more enemies -- during the boss fight. Players can still ignore the XP dots if they prefer to do so, but now it'll take much longer and be more challenging to defeat the boss while playing this way.[/p][p]Please let me know your thoughts either in the comments or in the [url="https://trampolinetales.com/discord"]official discord[/url]![/p][p]-Dan[/p][h1]Bug Fixes[/h1][list][*][p]Fixed a bug where unmuting the game after starting a run but before moving would still cause music to play[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed a bug where the game could lag if a few hundred Toothpicks were active at the same time[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed a typo in the Turkish translation[/p][/*][/list]

notes.title: The Garden Update
notes.content: [p]The game has been patched to add a new maze, new upgrades, upgrade balancing, community items, and more![/p][p][/p][h1]News[/h1][p]Hey everyone! As previously announced, this is the penultimate content patch for Maze Mice. The next content patch will coincide with the game exiting Early Access. You can read more about that here if you missed it:[/p][p][dynamiclink href="https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/3385370/view/518589674441148930"][/dynamiclink][/p][h1]New Content[/h1][list][*][p]Added another unlockable maze[/p][/*][*][p]Added 3 more unlockable upgrades[/p][/*][*][p]Added a music track for the boss fight[/p][/*][*][p]Added a longest game stat[/p][/*][*][p]Added an auto-pick button (it appears when the upgrade pool is limited to 2 or less upgrades)[/p][/*][*][p]Added Steam trading cards and community items[/p][/*][/list][p][/p][h1]Game Balance[/h1][list][*][p]Boomerang's base damage is now 500 (instead of 400)[/p][/*][*][p]Boomerang's damage increment is now 250 (instead of 200)[/p][/*][*][p]Boomerang's XP gain is now 2.5% (instead of 5%)[/p][/*][*][p]Fleas' base damage is now 3 (instead of 4)[/p][/*][*][p]Marbles' cooldown is now 9 seconds (instead of 10 seconds)[/p][/*][*][p]Recycling's cooldown is now 25 seconds (instead of 30 seconds)[/p][/*][*][p]Recycling's cooldown decrement is now 2.5 seconds (instead of 3 seconds)[/p][/*][*][p]Rubber Band's damage increment is now 125 (instead of 100)[/p][/*][*][p]Snowball's base damage increase is now 0.2% (instead of 0.1%)[/p][/*][*][p]Sunflower Seeds' cooldown is now 40 seconds (instead of 30 seconds)[/p][/*][*][p]Sunflower Seeds' cooldown decrement is now 4 seconds (instead of 3 seconds)[/p][/*][*][p]Thumbtacks' ammo increment is now 20 (instead of 15)[/p][/*][*][p]Toothpicks' base damage is now 5 (instead of 8)[/p][/*][*][p]Toothpicks' damage increment is now 5 (instead of 8)[/p][/*][*][p]Toothpicks' cooldown is now 12 seconds (instead of 10 seconds)[/p][/*][*][p]Zen now only appears if 5 or more upgrade slots are filled[/p][/*][/list][p][/p][h1]Balance Reasoning[/h1][p]Boomerang made gaining multiple levels more trivial than I would like. Reducing the XP gain while increasing the damage will make the upgrade a bit more risky to take at early levels, while still being strong at later levels.[/p][p]Fleas were able to deal a large amount of damage to the boss very quickly if obtained early in a run. Reducing the upgrade's base damage by even a single point will help bring it in line due to its exponential nature.[/p][p]Marbles and Recycling were less powerful than I'd like them to be, but not by a large amount. Slightly reducing their cooldowns will make them more viable. The same goes for the damage increases for Rubber Band and Snowball, as well as the ammo upgrade for Thumbtacks.[/p][p]Sunflower Seeds made it too easy to effectively stockpile HP above the player's maximum HP. While this strategy is still something I'd like to allow, increasing the cooldown of the upgrade will prevent it from being too powerful.[/p][p]Toothpicks could easily make the boss fight trivial, while still frequently one-shotting enemies at early levels. It's for this reason that they've received the most drastic nerf among all the upgrades changed.[/p][p]Zen was frustrating to see when the player had only a few upgrade slots filled. I suspect making Zen only appear with 6 or 7 upgrade slots filled would be too powerful, so this is a good middle ground.[/p][p]Please let me know your thoughts either in the comments or in the [url="https://trampolinetales.com/discord"]official discord[/url]![/p][p]-Dan[/p]

notes.title: Maze Mice's Development Roadmap and v1.0 Release Date
notes.content: [p]Maze Mice will receive The Garden Update on June 20th at 1PM EST and will exit Early Access with The Dream Update on July 11th at 1PM EST.[/p][h1]News[/h1][p]Hey everyone! First off, thank you to all the wonderful people who have played Maze Mice while it's been in Early Access. Your feedback has been vital to making the game the best it can be. That being said, the game won't be in Early Access for much longer, as the majority of the game's unreleased content will be ready much sooner than I expected![/p][h1]Upcoming Content[/h1][list][*][p]2 mazes (the second of which has a layout that changes during gameplay)[/p][/*][*][p]3 upgrades (1 weapon, 2 utility)[/p][/*][*][p]~150 achievements (these will unlock retroactively)[/p][/*][*][p]A music track for the boss fight[/p][/*][*][p]An auto-pick button[/p][/*][*][p]Steam trading cards[/p][/*][*][p]Upgrade balancing[/p][/*][/list][p]These updates will bring the game to the state that I promised it would be at by the end of Early Access, and then some.[/p][p]After exiting Early Access, Maze Mice [i]might[/i] receive some more content updates, but it is not incredibly likely as the game is still very far from making back what it cost to have it made. This might change though, you never know! I might do a blog post down the line breaking down the game's budget, so consider [url="https://blog.trampolinetales.com/"]subscribing to my newsletter[/url] if you're interested in seeing that.[/p][p]As always, thank you for reading and for your continued support of my work. If you have any questions, feel free to ask them and I'll do my best to answer.[/p][p]-Dan[/p]

notes.title: Pac-Man meets a time-stopping survivor-like bullet heaven in Maze Mice out in Early Access
notes.content:
Maze Mice is the latest game from the developer of the popular Luck be a Landlord, and while many developers continue making their own form of Vampire Survivor-like, this is probably the most unique so far that truly mixes things up as it feels a lot more like Pac-Man.

Read the full article here: https://www.gamingonlinux.com/2025/05/pac-man-meets-a-time-stopping-survivor-like-bullet-heaven-in-maze-mice-out-in-early-access/

notes.title: Maze Mice is out now!
notes.content:
Maze Mice is out now!

[previewyoutube=EHFA0JTCG9c;full][/previewyoutube]

After the success of my previous game, [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1404850/Luck_be_a_Landlord/]Luck be a Landlord[/url], I was unsure if I even had it in me to make another game.

Now that Maze Mice is available in Early Access, I know I was wrong and I have plenty more games I would love to make.

Thank you for being a part of this journey with me, and I'm so thrilled to bring my next game to you.

Also, you may notice that the number of characters and upgrades in the game is actually [b]double[/b] what I initially advertised. If you're curious as to why that is, you can read more about it [url=https://blog.trampolinetales.com/a-really-big-change-to-maze-mices-release-its-a-good-thing/]on my blog post here[/url].
